Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map n55-n68 only (terminal model branch). Read numbered ranges, cover named declarations. Return JSON.

1	//! The primary terminal emulation structure. This represents a single
     2	//! "terminal" containing a grid of characters and exposes various operations
     3	//! on that grid. This also maintains the scrollback buffer.
     4	const Terminal = @This();
     5	
     6	const std = @import("std");
     7	const build_options = @import("terminal_options");
     8	const lib = @import("lib.zig");
     9	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    10	const tripwire = @import("../tripwire.zig");
    11	const testing = std.testing;
    12	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    13	const simd = @import("../simd/main.zig");
    14	const unicode = @import("../unicode/main.zig");
    15	const uucode = @import("uucode");
    16	
    17	const ansi = @import("ansi.zig");
    18	const modespkg = @import("modes.zig");
    19	const charsets = @import("charsets.zig");
    20	const xt_checksum = @import("xt_checksum.zig");
    21	const csi = @import("csi.zig");
    22	const hyperlink = @import("hyperlink.zig");
    23	const glyph = @import("apc/glyph.zig");
    24	const kitty = @import("kitty.zig");
    25	const osc = @import("osc.zig");
    26	const point = @import("point.zig");
    27	const sgr = @import("sgr.zig");
    28	const Tabstops = @import("Tabstops.zig");
    29	const color = @import("color.zig");
    30	const mouse = @import("mouse.zig");
    31	const Stream = @import("stream_terminal.zig").Stream;
    32	
    33	const size = @import("size.zig");
    34	const pagepkg = @import("page.zig");
    35	const style = @import("style.zig");
    36	const PageList = @import("PageList.zig");
    37	const Screen = @import("Screen.zig");
    38	const ScreenSet = @import("ScreenSet.zig");
    39	const Page = pagepkg.Page;
    40	const Cell = pagepkg.Cell;
    41	const Row = pagepkg.Row;
    42	
    43	const log = std.log.scoped(.terminal);
    44	
    45	/// Default tabstop interval
    46	const TABSTOP_INTERVAL = 8;
    47	
    48	/// The set of screens behind this terminal (e.g. primary vs alternate).
    49	screens: ScreenSet,
    50	
    51	/// Whether we're currently writing to the status line (DECSASD and DECSSDT).
    52	/// We don't support a status line currently so we just black hole this
    53	/// data so that it doesn't mess up our main display.
    54	status_display: ansi.StatusDisplay = .main,
    55	
    56	/// Where the tabstops are.
    57	tabstops: Tabstops,
    58	
    59	/// The size of the terminal.
    60	rows: size.CellCountInt,
    61	cols: size.CellCountInt,
    62	
    63	/// The size of the screen in pixels. This is used for pty events and images
    64	width_px: u32 = 0,
    65	height_px: u32 = 0,
    66	
    67	/// The current scrolling region.
    68	scrolling_region: ScrollingRegion,
    69	
    70	/// The last reported pwd, if any.
    71	pwd: std.ArrayList(u8),
    72	
    73	/// The title of the terminal as set by escape sequences (e.g. OSC 0/2).
    74	title: std.ArrayList(u8),
    75	
    76	/// The color state for this terminal.
    77	colors: Colors,
    78	
    79	/// The previous printed character. This is used for the repeat previous
    80	/// char CSI (ESC [ <n> b).
    81	previous_char: ?u21 = null,
    82	
    83	/// The modes that this terminal currently has active.
    84	modes: modespkg.ModeState = .{},
    85	
    86	/// Terminal-level cursor state.
    87	cursor: Cursor = .{},
    88	
    89	/// The checksum variant DECRQCRA computes after RIS or DECSTR. The current
    90	/// variant is in `flags.xt_checksum`.
    91	default_xt_checksum: xt_checksum.Flags = .{},
    92	
    93	/// The most recently set mouse shape for the terminal.
    94	mouse_shape: mouse.Shape = .text,
    95	
    96	/// Per-session Glyph Protocol registrations.
    97	glyph_glossary: glyph.Glossary = .empty,
    98	
    99	/// Kitty drag and drop protocol (OSC 72) state. Allocated when a client
   100	/// registers to accept drops (t=a) and freed when it unregisters (t=A),
   101	/// so a terminal that never runs a drag and drop aware program pays
   102	/// nothing for it. Non-null means a client currently accepts drops.
   103	kitty_dnd: ?*kitty.dnd.State = null,
   104	
   105	/// These are just a packed set of flags we may set on the terminal.
   106	flags: packed struct {
   107	    // This supports a Kitty extension where programs using semantic
   108	    // prompts (OSC133) can annotate their new prompts with `redraw=0` to
   109	    // disable clearing the prompt on resize.
   110	    shell_redraws_prompt: osc.semantic_prompt.Redraw = .true,
   111	
   112	    // This is set via ESC[4;2m. Any other modify key mode just sets
   113	    // this to false and we act in mode 1 by default.
   114	    modify_other_keys_2: bool = false,
   115	
   116	    /// The mouse event mode and format. These are set to the last
   117	    /// set mode in modes. You can't get the right event/format to use
   118	    /// based on modes alone because modes don't show you what order
   119	    /// this was called so we have to track it separately.
   120	    mouse_event: mouse.Event = .none,
   121	    mouse_format: mouse.Format = .x10,
   122	
   123	    /// Set via the XTSHIFTESCAPE sequence. If true (XTSHIFTESCAPE = 1)
   124	    /// then we want to capture the shift key for the mouse protocol
   125	    /// if the configuration allows it.
   126	    mouse_shift_capture: enum(u2) { null, false, true } = .null,
   127	
   128	    /// The checksum variant DECRQCRA computes, set via XTCHECKSUM.
   129	    xt_checksum: xt_checksum.Flags = .{},
   130	
   131	    /// True if the window is focused.
   132	    focused: bool = true,
   133	
   134	    /// True if the terminal view may be visible. Unknown visibility is
   135	    /// represented as visible so callers behave conservatively.
   136	    visible: bool = true,
   137	
   138	    /// Whether a resize may pull rows out of scrollback back into the
   139	    /// active area. This should be false if the pty keeps its own screen
   140	    /// buffer without scrollback (e.g. Windows ConPTY) so that we stay in
   141	    /// sync with it. See PageList.Resize for details. This is configuration
   142	    /// rather than terminal state so it is preserved across a full reset.
   143	    resize_pull_scrollback: bool = true,
   144	
   145	    /// True if the terminal is in a password entry mode. This is set
   146	    /// to true based on termios state. This is set
   147	    /// to true based on termios state.
   148	    password_input: bool = false,
   149	
   150	    /// True if the terminal should perform selection scrolling.
   151	    selection_scroll: bool = false,
   152	
   153	    /// Dirty flag used only by the search thread. The renderer is expected
   154	    /// to set this to true if the viewport was dirty as it was rendering.
   155	    /// This is used by the search thread to more efficiently re-search the
   156	    /// viewport and active area.
   157	    ///
   158	    /// Since the renderer is going to inspect the viewport/active area ANYWAYS,
   159	    /// this lets our search thread do less work and hold the lock less time,
   160	    /// resulting in more throughput for everything.
   161	    search_viewport_dirty: bool = false,
   162	
   163	    /// Dirty flags for the renderer.
   164	    dirty: Dirty = .{},
   165	} = .{},

   167	/// The various color configurations a terminal maintains and that can
   168	/// be set dynamically via OSC, with defaults usually coming from a
   169	/// configuration.
   170	pub const Colors = struct {
   171	    background: color.DynamicRGB,
   172	    foreground: color.DynamicRGB,
   173	    cursor: color.DynamicRGB,
   174	    palette: color.DynamicPalette,
   175	
   176	    pub const default: Colors = .{
   177	        .background = .unset,
   178	        .foreground = .unset,
   179	        .cursor = .unset,
   180	        .palette = .default,
   181	    };
   182	};
   183	
   184	/// Returns the current color for an xterm OSC color target.
   185	///
   186	/// Unsupported dynamic and special colors return null. The cursor color
   187	/// follows xterm-style reporting and falls back to the foreground color when
   188	/// no explicit cursor color is set.
   189	pub fn colorForXterm(self: *const Terminal, target: osc.color.Target) ?color.RGB {
   190	    return switch (target) {
   191	        .palette => |i| self.colors.palette.current[i],
   192	        .dynamic => |dynamic| switch (dynamic) {
   193	            .foreground => self.colors.foreground.get(),
   194	            .background => self.colors.background.get(),
   195	            .cursor => self.colors.cursor.get() orelse
   196	                self.colors.foreground.get(),
   197	            .pointer_foreground,
   198	            .pointer_background,

    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {
   182	                    // The encoded data was produced by our codec and remains
   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");

    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real

    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.

    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///

    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.

   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }

   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},

   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };

   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );

   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {

   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.

   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");

35	backend: termio.Backend,
    36	
    37	/// The derived configuration for this termio implementation.
    38	config: DerivedConfig,
    39	
    40	/// The terminal emulator internal state. This is the abstract "terminal"
    41	/// that manages input, grid updating, etc. and is renderer-agnostic. It
    42	/// just stores internal state about a grid.
    43	terminal: terminalpkg.Terminal,
    44	
    45	/// The shared render state
    46	renderer_state: *renderer.State,
    47	
    48	/// A handle to wake up the renderer. This hints to the renderer that
    49	/// a repaint should happen.
    50	renderer_wakeup: xev.Async,
    51	
    52	/// The mailbox for notifying the renderer of things.
    53	renderer_mailbox: *renderer.Thread.Mailbox,
    54	
    55	/// The mailbox for communicating with the surface.
    56	surface_mailbox: apprt.surface.Mailbox,
    57	
    58	/// The cached size info
    59	size: renderer.Size,
    60	
    61	/// The mailbox implementation to use.
    62	mailbox: termio.Mailbox,
    63	
    64	/// The stream parser. This parses the stream of escape codes and so on
    65	/// from the child process and calls callbacks in the stream handler.
    66	terminal_stream: StreamHandler.Stream,
    67	
    68	/// Last time the cursor was reset. This is used to prevent message
    69	/// flooding with cursor resets.
    70	last_cursor_reset: ?std.Io.Timestamp = null,
    71	
    72	/// State we have for thread enter. This may be null if we don't need
    73	/// to keep track of any state or if its already been freed.
    74	thread_enter_state: ?*ThreadEnterState = null,
    75	
    76	/// The state we need to keep around only until we enter the IO
    77	/// thread. Then we can throw it all away.
   250	/// Initialize the termio state.
   251	///
   252	/// This will also start the child process if the termio is configured
   253	/// to run a child process.
   254	pub fn init(self: *Termio, alloc: Allocator, opts: termio.Options) !void {
   255	    // The default terminal modes based on our config.
   256	    const default_modes: terminalpkg.ModePacked = modes: {
   257	        var modes: terminalpkg.ModePacked = .{};
   258	
   259	        // Setup our initial grapheme cluster support if enabled. We use a
   260	        // switch to ensure we get a compiler error if more cases are added.
   261	        switch (opts.full_config.@"grapheme-width-method") {
   262	            .unicode => modes.grapheme_cluster = true,
   263	            .legacy => {},
   264	        }
   265	
   266	        // Set default cursor blink settings
   267	        modes.cursor_blinking = opts.config.cursor_blink orelse true;
   268	
   269	        break :modes modes;
   270	    };
   271	
   272	    // Create our terminal
   273	    var term = try terminalpkg.Terminal.init(global.io(), alloc, opts: {
   274	        const grid_size = opts.size.grid();
   275	        break :opts .{
   276	            .cols = grid_size.columns,
   277	            .rows = grid_size.rows,
   278	            .max_scrollback_bytes = opts.full_config.@"scrollback-limit-bytes".optional(),
   279	            .max_scrollback_lines = opts.full_config.@"scrollback-limit-lines".optional(),
   280	            .default_modes = default_modes,
   281	            .default_cursor_style = opts.config.cursor_style,
   282	            .default_cursor_blink = opts.config.cursor_blink,
   283	            .default_xt_checksum = opts.config.xt_checksum_extension,
   284	            .colors = .{
   285	                .background = .init(opts.config.background.toTerminalRGB()),
   286	                .foreground = .init(opts.config.foreground.toTerminalRGB()),
   287	                .cursor = cursor: {
   288	                    const color = opts.config.cursor_color orelse break :cursor .unset;
   289	                    const rgb = color.toTerminalRGB() orelse break :cursor .unset;
   290	                    break :cursor .init(rgb);
   291	                },
   292	                .palette = .default,
   293	            },
   294	            .kitty_image_storage_limit = opts.config.image_storage_limit,
   295	            .kitty_image_loading_limits = .allWithTempDir(global.tmpDirPath()),
   296	        };
   297	    });
   298	    errdefer term.deinit(alloc);
   299	
   300	    // The default palette may be an allocator-owned copy, so it is set
   301	    // once the terminal owns its memory and can release it on deinit.
   302	    try term.colors.palette.changeDefault(alloc, opts.config.palette);
   303	
   304	    // Setup our terminal size in pixels for certain requests.
   305	    term.width_px = term.cols * opts.size.cell.width;
   306	    term.height_px = term.rows * opts.size.cell.height;
   307	
   308	    // Setup our backend.
   309	    var backend = opts.backend;
   310	    backend.initTerminal(&term);
   311	
   312	    // Create our stream handler. This points to memory in self so it
   313	    // isn't safe to use until self.* is set.
   314	    const handler: StreamHandler = .{
   315	        .alloc = alloc,
   316	        .termio_mailbox = &self.mailbox,
   317	        .surface_mailbox = opts.surface_mailbox,
   318	        .renderer_state = opts.renderer_state,
   319	        .renderer_wakeup = opts.renderer_wakeup,
   320	        .renderer_mailbox = opts.renderer_mailbox,
   321	        .size = &self.size,
   322	        .terminal = &self.terminal,
   323	        .osc_color_report_format = opts.config.osc_color_report_format,
   324	        .clipboard_write = opts.config.clipboard_write,
   325	        .clipboard_write_limit = opts.config.clipboard_write_limit,
   326	        .enquiry_response = opts.config.enquiry_response,
   327	        .xt_checksum_report = opts.config.xt_checksum_report,
   328	    };
   329	
   330	    const thread_enter_state = try ThreadEnterState.create(
   331	        alloc,
   332	        opts.full_config,
   333	    );
   334	
   335	    self.* = .{
   336	        .alloc = alloc,
   337	        .terminal = term,
   338	        .config = opts.config,
   339	        .renderer_state = opts.renderer_state,
   340	        .renderer_wakeup = opts.renderer_wakeup,
   341	        .renderer_mailbox = opts.renderer_mailbox,
   342	        .surface_mailbox = opts.surface_mailbox,
   343	        .size = opts.size,
   344	        .backend = backend,
   345	        .mailbox = opts.mailbox,
   346	        .terminal_stream = .init(.{
   347	            .allocator = alloc,
   348	            .handler = handler,
   349	        }),
   350	        .thread_enter_state = thread_enter_state,
   351	    };
   352	}
   353	
   354	pub fn deinit(self: *Termio) void {
   355	    self.backend.deinit();

1	//! The primary terminal emulation structure. This represents a single
     2	//! "terminal" containing a grid of characters and exposes various operations
     3	//! on that grid. This also maintains the scrollback buffer.
     4	const Terminal = @This();
     5

     7	const build_options = @import("terminal_options");
     8	const lib = @import("lib.zig");
     9	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    10	const tripwire = @import("../tripwire.zig");

   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains

   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page

   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };

   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},

   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.

   161	    ///

   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.

   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {

   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );

   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {

   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
